notes: §1985:X.5.5.3 SR1 says 'The availability of the multiple file-names and the EXTEND phrase is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module, Relative I-O module, or Indexed I-O module supported by the implementation'; the compiler implements the high subset (§1985:I.1.5.1; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md: every required module at its highest level), so both are available at 85 for every organization. The grammar's useOnTarget takes fileName+ or EXTEND at every edition and ProcedureTableBuilder.DeclBindUse binds a file list (each file resolved, sort-merge files refused) or the EXTEND open mode (once per procedure division, COBOL0897). Probed at 85 (classes b, c, e): one USE on a sequential, a relative and an indexed file fires for the at-end READ of each, and the next statement runs (D1 10 00 00 / AFTER S1 ... D1 10 10 10 / AFTER I1); USE ON EXTEND fires for a failed OPEN EXTEND of a relative file (D2 EXTEND 35, then AFTER EXTEND 35); the witness's USE GLOBAL ON F1 F2 and ON EXTEND print its .out; EXTEND twice draws COBOL0897, ON F1 EXTEND COBOL2269, ON with no operand COBOL0001, USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O COBOL0877/0878 and USE without PROCEDURE COBOL0900.

next.reason: 1985: "The availability of the multiple file-names and the EXTEND phrase is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module"; 2023: "No such dependency: the 14.9.49.3 USE rules allow file-names and EXTEND with no I-O module level, and 2023 defines no module levels". 2023 has no module levels. The USE candidates cover file-names and EXTEND without any availability dependency, so the level-dependence requirement is dropped.
